usda.source_layer: CSB1825.gdb / national1825 (CRS: NAD83 Conus Albers, equivalent to EPSG:5070)
usda.licence: Public domain (USDA NASS: 'provided to the public as is and are considered public domain and free to redistribute')
usda.attribution: Field boundaries: USDA NASS Crop Sequence Boundaries 2018-2025 (public domain)
usda.crop_legend: CDL2018..CDL2025 codes mapped to names using the full Cropland Data Layer category list (135 codes) from the data dictionary in NationalCSB_2018-2025_rev23_metadata.htm shipped inside the zip; no unmapped codes occurred
usda.clipping: Attribute filter STATEFIPS = '19' AND CNTYFIPS = '169' on the national layer (6027 source polygons, cross-checked against a bbox read). No geometric clipping; polygons are whole CSB fields as assigned to Story County by NASS.
processing: Reprojected NAD83 Albers -> WGS84 lon/lat with PROJ (pyproj 3.7.1); NAD83 treated as WGS84 (no datum shift, ~1 m)
180 source polygons were invalid (self-intersections) and were repaired with GEOS make_valid, keeping polygonal parts
Coordinates rounded to 5 decimals (6 decimals gave 5.85 MB)
Redundant collinear vertices removed with a 0.01 m Douglas-Peucker tolerance in the source Albers CRS (a 1 m tolerance gave no meaningful further reduction, so it was not used)
Exterior rings counter-clockwise (RFC 7946); fields < 1 acre dropped (none were)
acres = geodesic area on the WGS84 ellipsoid of the published geometry (pyproj Geod), 1 decimal; agrees with NASS CSBACRES within 0.4 acre

ai.dataset: Fields of The World (FTW) - Global field boundaries, PRUE model on Sentinel-2 (vectors 'alpha', results-by-admin-conf)
ai.version: predictions/vectors/alpha, partition US_IA (fiboa GeoParquet with confidence column)
ai.attribution: AI field boundaries: Fields of The World (Taylor Geospatial et al.), CC BY 4.0
ai.citation: Robinson, C. et al. (2026). The first global agricultural field boundary map at 10 m resolution. arXiv:2605.11055
ai.clipping: Kept 2025 predictions (determination:datetime year) whose bbox intersects the Story County outline, then only polygons whose centroid lies inside the Census TIGER/Line 2024 county polygon GEOID 19169 (3797 polygons); 388 under 1 acre dropped. Polygons are not cut at the county line.
processing: Coordinates rounded to 5 decimals (6 decimals gave 7.69 MB); simplification at 0.01 m and 1 m was tried but did not shrink the file (10 m raster stair-step outlines have no redundant vertices), so geometry is otherwise unmodified. File remains above the ~4 MB target.
acres = geodesic area on the WGS84 ellipsoid, 1 decimal
id = ai-<n>, numbered in order of the upstream FTW id
notes: confidence (0-100, FTW-derived from the 500 m confidence COG) is null for every field in Story County: per the dataset README, null means the field lies outside the modelled-confidence layer's coverage, not a low score
FTW polygons are remote-sensing field units (connected field pixels at 10 m), not legal parcels; 2024 predictions are also available in the same file
